operations.name: signed_checkpoint
operations.notes: Runtime-dependent on TypeScript: the NAPI-backed (Node/Bun) TS runtime signs the canonical checkpoint payload in-process AND the TS SDK surfaces the resulting Ed25519 signature on Checkpoint.signature (mapped through bindings/typescript/src/internal/native.ts), so typescript:true is honest for the default runtime. This WASM-vs-native difference is recorded as an ADR-048 §7b cross-bridge semantic divergence for event_log_checkpoint*; the row stays true because the primary NAPI-backed runtime signs and surfaces the signature, while the WASM fallback returns the unsigned payload hash.

operations.name: shutdown_timeout
operations.notes: SCP.shutdown(timeout) — bounded graceful shutdown replacing the Phase 4 PR 1 terminal infallible shutdown. Propagates a tokio_util::sync::CancellationToken into every long-running task, waits on a JoinSet up to the timeout, and forcibly cancels anything still running at the deadline. Async across all non-WASM bridges: PyO3 returns a coroutine, NAPI returns Promise<void>, UniFFI generates Kotlin suspend fun / Swift async throws. Timeout is carried as u64 milliseconds across all three bridges (NAPI was widened from u32 in #1692). Each SDK wrapper clamps to its bridge's maximum at the boundary. See ADR-048 §Decision 5 and §Notes/Shutdown-timeout integer width across FFI bridges.

exemptions.wasm: No long-lived native runtime to drain on WASM.

operations.name: suspend
operations.notes: Disconnects transport and marks BridgeInstance as suspended for mobile/desktop backgrounding. No-op on WASM (no long-lived native runtime). All three FFI bridges (PyO3 scp_suspend, NAPI scpSuspend, UniFFI scpSuspend) call BridgeInstance::suspend. Phase 4 PR 4 (#1549) deleted the free-function SDK wrappers; SCP.suspend() is now the only entry point in every SDK: Python scp.suspend(), TypeScript scp.suspend(), Kotlin scp.suspend(), Swift scp.suspend().

operations.name: resume
operations.notes: ASYNC as of Phase 4 PR 3 (#1678, 2026-04-18) — BREAKING CHANGE. BridgeInstanceCore::resume is async fn; per-bridge overrides reconnect every pending relay URL and restore persisted contexts before returning. Reconnect failures surface as LifecycleError::ReconnectFailed { url, reason }. All three FFI bridges expose the async path: PyO3 releases the GIL and block_ons, NAPI returns a Promise, UniFFI generates Kotlin suspend fun / Swift async throws. Phase 4 PR 4 (#1549) deleted the free-function SDK wrappers; SCP.resume() is now the only entry point in every SDK: Python async def resume(), TypeScript scp.resume(): Promise<void>, Kotlin scp.resume() (suspend fun), Swift func resume() async throws. WASM is a no-op (no long-lived native runtime).

operations.name: with_storage_sqlite
operations.notes: SCP.withStorage(Sqlite { path, key }) exposes the SQLCipher-backed SqliteStorage across all three non-WASM bridges (#1491, #1260; Phase 4 PR 3, 2026-04-18). The StorageConfig::Sqlite key field is a SqliteKeyMaterial sum type accepting EITHER raw key material (Raw, 32-byte key validated at the FFI boundary) OR a passphrase (Passphrase, SQLCipher key derived via Argon2id with a persisted per-database salt sidecar). For sqlite, exactly ONE of key/passphrase must be supplied — both or neither is a ValidationError; both forms are wrapped in Zeroizing. PyO3 accepts Python bytes (key) or a str (passphrase); NAPI accepts a hex string OR Uint8Array (key) or a string (passphrase); UniFFI generates Swift StorageConfig.sqlite(path:key:) / SqliteKeyMaterial.raw|.passphrase and the Kotlin equivalents via #[derive(uniffi::Enum)]. SDK convenience constructors: Swift SCP.withStorage(sqliteDir:key:)/passphrase variant, Kotlin SCP.withSqlite(dir, key)/passphrase variant, Python SCP.with_storage({...}), TypeScript SCP.withStorage({...}). The Supervisor's mls_storage view, context-snapshot persistence, and event log all share a single rusqlite::Connection via the one Arc<SqliteStorage>.

operations.name: add_relay_url
operations.notes: CoreFields::relay_url (Mutex<Option<String>>) replaced with relay_urls (Mutex<HashSet<String>>) in Phase 4 PR 3 (#1678, 2026-04-18). New accessors add_relay_url / remove_relay_url / pending_relay_urls; each per-bridge resume() iterates the HashSet and reconnects each URL. First reconnect failure surfaces as LifecycleError::ReconnectFailed { url, reason }; successfully-connected URLs remain in the pending set for retry.

call_invariants.description: The runtime `enforce_send_economy` helper must delegate to the unified `enforce_economy` function (economy.rs). Skipping delegation would let `ContextManager::send_message` bypass budget/velocity/UCAN checks for paid contexts.

`ContextManager::import_context` must call `validate_export_for_import` before touching event log or crypto state. Skipping validation lets a malformed or malicious snapshot install a broken MLS group or corrupt the Merkle chain.

Every non-WASM bridge's `identity_create` entrypoint must call `ensure_did_resolver_initialized_on` before returning. The resolver is a per-bridge-instance slot used by UCAN validation (#311, ADR-048 renamed the helper from `ensure_did_resolver_initialized` to the `_on` suffix convention for per-instance helpers in Phase 4 PR 5); skipping initialization degrades UCAN verification to string-only lookups. WASM is exempt per ADR-034 (BridgeDidResolver stays in-process).

exemptions.wasm: ADR-034: WASM bridge uses BridgeDidResolver directly (string-only resolver, no tokio runtime) — no ensure_did_resolver_initialized_on to precede.
